rationale: After the trabeculodysgenesis anatomy block, checks understanding of the embryological mechanism before moving to examination findings.
After the management block emphasising surgery as first-line, tests application of the treatment principle rather than medical therapy.
After the investigation block covering IOP, disc, and fields, tests ability to analyse the clinical triad for POAG diagnosis.

Critical POAG-vs-PACG management distinction: after the POAG management block, directly reinforces that prostaglandin analogues are first-line in POAG, contrasting with the pilocarpine+acetazolamide+mannitol emergency protocol in PACG.
After the pupil block pathophysiology block, checks understanding of the anatomical mechanism before moving to examination findings.
POAG-vs-PACG management distinction: directly tests emergency management of acute PACG vs chronic POAG management — the critical clinical distinction required.
After the pathophysiological framework block, checks understanding of the open-angle vs closed-angle mechanistic scaffold for secondary glaucomas.
After the named secondary glaucoma catalogue block, tests ability to distinguish between the two lens-induced glaucomas (phacomorphic vs phacolytic) which are mechanistically opposite.
After the counselling technique block, checks understanding of the key communication principle that makes glaucoma counselling uniquely challenging — the asymptomatic nature of the disease.
After the applied counselling scenarios block, tests ability to apply counselling principles to a non-adherent patient — the most common and high-stakes scenario in glaucoma practice.
